answer: Anchor each identity to a rated-chess record: a verified Elo from hundreds of rated games against opponents, spread over months. The grove is the trust base: a sparrow with no games carries no weight; voting power grows with games played. The kernel is the game log - timestamps, opponents, move times. A farmer with one hundred puppets must play one hundred schedules in real time, paying entry fees and months of time, while identical opening repertoires collapse the puppets into one record. Honest players pay once, their own games; a Sybil farm pays per puppet, per game, forever.
